name: Finance: Out-of-sample equity-premium prediction
description: Forecast next month's US equity premium (the log S&P 500 return over the T-bill rate) from the Welch-Goyal predictors observed up to the forecast origin. The evaluator recomputes the out-of-sample R^2 against the prevailing historical mean over 732 monthly forecasts from 1965-01 to 2025-12.

sources.locator: Welch and Goyal (2008): predictor definitions, recursive out-of-sample forecasts against the prevailing mean, one-month publication lag for inflation (Sections 1-5, Table 3 for monthly data).
Campbell and Thompson (2008): out-of-sample R^2 against the historical average and economically motivated forecast restrictions.
Goyal, Welch and Zafirov (2024): updated and revised predictor data and evidence through 2021; the data file used here extends it to 2025.
Amit Goyal's data page: updated Welch-Goyal monthly predictor data to 2025-12 (file pinned by SHA-256 in catalog/finance-data-lock.json).

requirements.datasets: Updated Welch-Goyal monthly predictor data (Amit Goyal, to 2025-12) fetched by scripts/prepare_finance.py and verified by SHA-256; not redistributed.

evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: forecast_premium(history) -> float: forecast of next month's log equity premium log(1+R_m) - log(1+R_f) (decimal, |forecast| <= 0.5). history is a dict of 1-D float arrays from 1871-01 through the forecast origin month t (NaN where a series is unavailable): the Welch-Goyal columns 'Index', 'D12', 'E12', 'b/m', 'tbl', 'AAA', 'BAA', 'lty', 'ntis', 'Rfree', 'infl', 'ltr', 'corpr', 'svar', 'csp', 'CRSP_SPvw', 'CRSP_SPvwx' (decimal rates; inflation of month t is withheld because the CPI is published with a lag), 'yyyymm' (integers) and 'equity_premium' (log excess return of each month, NaN before 1926-01). Called once per origin for the 732 targets 1965-01..2025-12. Score: Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 in percent against the prevailing mean of the equity premium since 1926-01 (maximize; the seed scores exactly 0). The candidate runs in a separate sandboxed process: numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas and the other installed packages are importable, while the evaluator's library, its data files, the network and subprocesses are not accessible; one thread and 3 GB of memory. It receives only the arguments described here, one call at a time: the arguments of a call are sent after the value of the previous call has been received. Arguments and return values travel as numbers, strings, lists, dicts with string keys and numeric numpy arrays, so a tuple arrives as a list

limitations: The evaluation months are public. A candidate that reads the prepared file, embeds remembered returns or is tuned on 1965-2025 can look ahead; the interface only passes data up to the origin. Treat scores as development scores and freeze a candidate before testing it on later months.

Monthly out-of-sample R^2 values in this literature are fractions of a percent with sampling error of the same order; the Clark-West statistic is reported, but a small positive score is not by itself evidence of predictability.

One data vintage (the 2025 update, which revises some historical series) is used as if it were available in real time; apart from the one-month inflation lag, publication delays and revisions of the predictors are not modelled.

The score uses log equity premia and the unadjusted out-of-sample R^2; it does not measure economic value (certainty-equivalent gains, trading costs or leverage limits), and csp is only available until 2002-12.

The candidate runs in a sandboxed child process that never receives later data, realised outcomes or reference solutions; module-level code still runs once in the evaluator process when the shared template imports the candidate, and outside macOS (kernel sandbox) deliberately hostile native code could bypass the file policy.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value exists for this exact protocol (log premia, targets 1965-01 to 2025-12, 2025 data vintage). Welch and Goyal (2008) and Goyal, Welch and Zafirov (2024) find negative out-of-sample R^2 for most single predictors; with Campbell-Thompson restrictions the best monthly values in Welch and Goyal's Table 3 are about 0.3% on 1927-2004 data, and Rapach, Strauss and Zhou (2010) report gains from combining forecasts. The prevailing-mean seed scores exactly 0.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Determine whether the US equity premium is predictable out of sample from valuation ratios, interest rates and other economic variables.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Return predictability is central to asset-pricing theory (time-varying risk premia) and to long-horizon investment decisions; decades of in-sample evidence fail out of sample, so forecasts that reliably beat the historical mean remain an open empirical question.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Look at The Empirical Performance of Equity Premium Prediction
papers.primary_goal: Assess whether variables proposed in the literature predict the equity premium in sample and out of sample.
papers.task_relation: The task uses the same predictor data (updated to 2025), recursive forecasts and prevailing-mean benchmark, scoring the out-of-sample R^2 of a candidate forecasting rule.

papers.title: Predicting Excess Stock Returns Out of Sample: Can Anything Beat the Historical Average?
papers.primary_goal: Determine whether predictors of excess stock returns beat the historical average out of sample, in particular under simple economic restrictions.
papers.task_relation: The task's score is the Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R^2 against the historical average.

science_relevance.reason: Both cited papers have equity-premium predictability as their main research question, which is exactly what the task measures.
